calls.reason: The forecast has no deadline. The only evidence is an inference-market paper showing concentration falling, which neither establishes the no-moat premise nor settles whether anyone ever reaches 90%.
2026 had not ended at evaluation, and the only evidence is a SpaceX drawdown after index entry that had mostly recovered. No aggregate losses for retail investors or index funds are documented.

Anthropic's S-1 confirms the market is intensely competitive, but no completed investment history shows how AI returns compare with costs for any developer. The claim concerns eventual outcomes with no end date.

Anthropic paused its Agent SDK billing change and raised some limits. A switching survey shows Claude improving but does not isolate pricing effects, so widespread customer reconsideration is neither shown nor ruled out.

Anthropic had only filed its S-1, and OpenAI had not listed. S&P kept its index rules unchanged, but Nasdaq fast entry still exists, so the sequence of index entry followed by losses has not played out.

Evidence is mixed. Anthropic cut Opus token prices, but a quality-adjusted price study finds the cost per completed task stopped falling. Neither the no-clear-winners premise nor monopoly margins are established.
